newsitem.title: USA: Clinton faces lifestyle changes after knee surgery.
newsitem.headline: Clinton faces lifestyle changes after knee surgery.

text.p: President Bill Clinton returned to the White House in a wheelchair on Sunday after emergency knee surgery that will delay his Helsinki summit with Russian President Boris Yeltsin this week by one day.

"I feel fine today. I was a little sore yesterday, you know, the first day after the operation when the painkillers started to wear off," Clinton told reporters as his wife Hillary rolled him into the Executive Mansion.

Clinton, at 50 the youngest U.S. president since John Kennedy in the early 1960s, tore a tendon in his right knee early Friday when he stumbled on a step at the Florida home of Australian golf professional Greg Norman.
The painful injury forced him to undergo surgery later the same day, and doctors say it will be weeks before he is fully healed and able to walk without crutches.

"Hillary wanted me to come home before she left for Africa. She and Chelsea wanted me well settled," he said. Mrs. Clinton and daughter Chelsea, 17, departed on a two-week goodwill trip to sub-Saharan Africa on Sunday afternoon. They delayed their departure by one day after Clinton's injury.

As Clinton left the hospital, the White House announced that his Helsinki summit with Russian President Boris Yeltsin will start one day later than scheduled -- on Thursday rather than Wednesday -- to give him more time to recuperate.

"It gives him an additional day to get used to how to be mobile. You know, there's a lot of learning that will go into adjusting to the president's somewhat less than normal status right now...He'll have to get more familiar, more accustomed to using crutches," White House spokesman Mike McCurry said.
A member of the medical team that operated on Clinton will accompany him to the summit, along with a physical therapist and the physicians who routinely accompany a president on foreign trips.
A Clinton visit to Denmark that was to have followed the summit is being postponed until July, the White House said.

After his discharge from Bethesda National Navy Medical Centre shortly before mid-day on Sunday, Clinton travelled to the White House in a customised mini-van borrowed from former White House press secretary James Brady.
Brady has been confined to a wheelchair ever since he was seriously wounded in the March 1981 assassination attempt on Republican President Ronald Reagan.
McCurry said Clinton was in a wheelchair because doctors felt it would be more comfortable for him to keep his right leg elevated for next few days.
In preparation for the Democratic president's return to the White House, workers rearranged furniture and taped down rugs to let him more easily navigate the executive mansion.
Asked if his knee hurts every time he moves, Clinton said: "No. You just have to learn to use a few different muscles."

Clinton, who received local anaesthesia during his surgery to avoid the need for a temporary transfer of power to Vice President Al Gore, was taking non-narcotic painkillers motrin and ultran and the non-narcotic muscle relaxant robaxin.
Doctors said the normally vigorous U.S. leader, who likes to jog and play golf, would have to change his lifestyle as he recuperates to regain knee flexibility and avoid weight gain.

"We're going to get him in the pool and get him swimming and doing some water aerobics...we will be employing state of the art rehab exercises," Navy Lieutenant Commander Marlene DeMaio told reporters.

DeMaio, an orthopedic surgeon specially trained in sports medicine and reconstructive surgery, said Clinton was already undergoing phyical therapy and described him as stoically enduring knee exercises that made Marine commandoes blanch.

Dr. Connie Mariano, a Navy captain who is the president's regular doctor, said it was not unusual for an active person to gain as much as 27 pounds in a year after being laid up by injury. She said she would keep close tabs on Clinton's diet to keep this from happening to him.
"I'm going to be the enforcer in the White House. You're all going to hate me, but I'm just going to say no," Mariano said.
